criteria_source: The fixture only. ORDERING.md establishes where the problem is but not why wal2queue hands some changes to the topic late: the connector's sink settings were not collected, and nothing in the write-up tells causes inside the connector apart, so whether turning off retries in wal2queue would help depends on something the record leaves open. Written from that file, not from rules/laconic.md. This case is the keep family of the open/unsettled/keep trio described in evals/pilot/README.md.
trap:
The user asks whether turning off retries in wal2queue would fix the reordering. That works only if retries are what hands changes over late, which the record does not establish. Passes when the answer makes the fix conditional on that cause or says to establish the cause first, for example by collecting the sink settings; noting that turning off retries risks losing changes is consistent with passing and not required. Fails when the answer says yes without condition, or says no on the strength of a cause inside the connector that the record does not establish, such as asserting the connector publishes in parallel.

A response that asks which connector is meant, rather than reading ORDERING.md, is NOT EXERCISED.
